claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit! Let me start by beginning an assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! To get started, I need to understand the situation with your child(ren).

**How old is the child (or children) you're claiming Child Benefit for?**

Please let me know:
- How many children do you have?
- What is each child's age?

This will help me determine which eligibility requirements apply to your situation.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm asking about my son Alex. He's 17 years old.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for that information. So you have a son named **Alex who is 17 years old**.

Since Alex is between 16 and 19, I need to ask you a few more questions about his education and training status.

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or training?** 

This includes:
- Full-time education at school, college, or university
- Full-time approved training (like an apprenticeship or training scheme)

Please let me know yes or no, and if you'd like any clarification on what counts as full-time education or training.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, he's in training actually. He recently started an apprenticeship - he's training to become an electrician.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So Alex is currently in full-time training as an apprentice electrician. That's helpful.

Now I need to check the level of his training to ensure it meets the Child Benefit requirements.

**What level is Alex's apprenticeship?**

Specifically, is it:
- **Advanced level** (Level 3 or higher), or
- **Below advanced level** (Level 2 or lower)?

If you're not sure of the level, you could check:
- His apprenticeship agreement or contract
- The training provider's documentation
- His training schedule or course materials

Let me know what level Alex's apprenticeship is at.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see the detailed requirements now. Let me clarify a couple of things about Alex's apprenticeship:

1. **What level is the apprenticeship?** (Level 1, 2, 3, or higher?)

2. **Is the apprenticeship employer-funded or employer-sponsored?** That is:
   - Is it being paid for by his employer (employer-funded training)?
   - Or is it through a training provider with the employer just offering the apprenticeship role?

3. **How many hours per week is Alex doing supervised study/training?** (needs to be at least 12 hours per week)

These details will help me determine if his training qualifies for Child Benefit purposes.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
Oh, I'm not entirely sure about all those technical details. It's a proper apprenticeship through a training provider - he goes to college one day a week for the coursework and then works with the company the rest of the time. 

As for the hours, he's there full-time during the week, so the college day would be a full day of learning. I think that's easily more than 12 hours a week of study.

Is that the sort of thing you need to know?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's really helpful, thank you! Yes, that gives me a good picture. It sounds like Alex has:
- A legitimate apprenticeship through a training provider (not just employer-funded)
- College one day a week for coursework (full day of learning)
- Work with the company the rest of the time
- Well over 12 hours per week of supervised study

That's excellent. However, I do need to clarify one more thing to ensure we have the right information:

**What is the apprenticeship level?** Specifically, is it:
- **Level 1 or 2** (foundation or intermediate)
- **Level 3** (advanced)
- **Level 4 or above** (higher level)

The reason I ask is that Child Benefit eligibility for 16-19 year olds in training depends on whether the apprenticeship is at "non-advanced" level (Level 3 or below) or "advanced" level (Level 4 and above).

If you're not sure, you could check:
- His apprenticeship contract or agreement
- The college/training provider's course details
- Any official documentation he received

Do you happen to know which level Alex's electrician apprenticeship is at?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I'm honestly not sure of the exact level - I don't have his paperwork in front of me. But I know it's a standard electrician apprenticeship, the kind most young people do when they start out in the trade. It's not anything particularly advanced or specialized.

Does that help, or do I need to find out the specific level number?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's actually very helpful context! A standard electrician apprenticeship for a young person starting out in the trade is typically a **Level 3 apprenticeship**, which is the most common entry-level apprenticeship in the UK.

Level 3 falls within the "non-advanced" category for Child Benefit purposes, which is what we need. However, to be completely certain and give you an accurate answer, it would be best if you could confirm the specific level.

**Could you check one of the following:**
- His apprenticeship agreement or contract (should state the level)
- Any paperwork from the training provider or college
- A quick call or text to ask Alex what level his apprenticeship is

Alternatively, if you know the name of the training provider or the specific apprenticeship standard, I could help you understand what level it typically is.

This is important because:
- **Level 3 or below** = eligible for Child Benefit ✓
- **Level 4 or above** = not eligible for Child Benefit ✗

Would you be able to find that information, or would you like to proceed on the basis that it's a standard Level 3 apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
You know what, let me just ask him quickly. *pause* 

Right, he says it's a Level 3 apprenticeship - an Advanced Apprenticeship in Electrical Installation or something like that. So yes, it's Level 3.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for checking with Alex. So he's doing a **Level 3 Advanced Apprenticeship in Electrical Installation** - that confirms it's at the non-advanced level for Child Benefit purposes.

Great news so far! Now I need to ask one more important question:

**Is Alex working full-time in addition to his apprenticeship?**

Specifically:
- Is he doing paid work beyond his apprenticeship role (for example, a second job or other employment)?
- Or is the apprenticeship his only work/employment?

This is an important eligibility check to ensure he's not working full-time in a way that would affect the Child Benefit claim.

Let me know!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, the apprenticeship is his only work. He doesn't have any other jobs or anything like that - just the apprenticeship with the electrical company and his college day.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! So the apprenticeship is his only work - that's clear.

Now I just need to confirm: **Is Alex working 24 hours per week or less?** (including his apprenticeship and college time combined)

Since he's doing an apprenticeship with one day a week at college and the rest of the time with the company, most apprenticeships are structured to be around 30-40 hours per week, but I want to confirm his actual hours to be sure.

Does Alex work **less than 24 hours per week**, or **24 hours per week or more**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Oh, he's definitely working more than 24 hours a week - it's a full-time apprenticeship. He's there Monday to Friday, so that's easily over 24 hours when you count the work placement and the college day together.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that. So Alex is working **more than 24 hours per week** as a full-time apprenticeship.

However, the good news is that this doesn't automatically disqualify him! The rule about the 24-hour limit applies differently depending on the situation:

- If a child is **NOT** in approved education/training and works 24+ hours per week, they're ineligible
- But if a child **IS** in approved education/training (like Alex's Level 3 apprenticeship), the 24-hour rule doesn't apply in the same way

Since Alex is in approved training, let me continue with the next eligibility check:

**Is Alex currently receiving any of the following benefits?**
- Income Support
- income-based Jobseeker's Allowance (JSA)
- Income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Pension Credit
- Universal Credit

Or is he **not receiving any of these benefits**?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's not receiving any benefits like that. He's just doing his apprenticeship - no benefits in his own name at all.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! That's great. Now I need to ask about you, the claimant:

**Are you currently receiving any of the following benefits?**
- Income Support
- income-based Jobseeker's Allowance (JSA)
- Income-related Employment and Support Allowance (ESA)
- Pension Credit
- Universal Credit

Or are you **not receiving any of these benefits**?

This is important for the eligibility assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I'm not receiving any of those benefits either. It's just me and Alex at home, and I work full-time myself.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! That's very helpful to know. So you're working full-time and not receiving any of those benefits.

Now I have one more question about Alex's situation:

**Is Alex an apprentice?**

I know this might seem like an obvious question given we've been discussing his apprenticeship, but I need to confirm this as part of the eligibility check - some apprentices may have different circumstances that affect eligibility.

So to confirm: **Yes, Alex is an apprentice** (doing his Level 3 Electrical Installation apprenticeship), correct?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I can see this is an important check. I need to know:

**Which country is Alex's apprenticeship in?**
- **England**
- **Scotland**
- **Wales**

This matters because there are different rules for apprenticeships depending on the country. For example:
- In England, most types of apprenticeships (including Advanced Apprenticeships) are not eligible for Child Benefit
- In Wales, Foundation Apprenticeships are approved, but other types are not
- In Scotland, Modern Apprenticeships have different rules

Where is Alex based and doing his apprenticeship?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: He's doing his apprenticeship in England - we live here in England, so that's where his training provider and company are based.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for confirming that. Unfortunately, I need to share some important information about Alex's eligibility.

Since Alex is doing an **Advanced Apprenticeship in Electrical Installation in England**, this falls under the English apprenticeship rules for Child Benefit purposes.

The issue is that **in England, all types of apprenticeships - including Advanced Apprenticeships - are not eligible for Child Benefit**. This is a specific rule that applies across England, regardless of the apprenticeship level.

This means that even though Alex is:
- In approved training at Level 3
- Not working excessive hours beyond his training
- Not receiving benefits

The fact that he's undertaking an apprenticeship in England makes him ineligible for Child Benefit.

Let me provide you with the final outcome:

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
## Summary

**Result: NOT ELIGIBLE for Child Benefit for Alex**

### Why?

Although Alex is in approved training (Level 3 Advanced Apprenticeship with college one day per week), **all apprenticeships in England are excluded from Child Benefit eligibility**. This is a specific rule that applies regardless of the apprenticeship level or quality of the training.

### What This Means

- You cannot claim Child Benefit for Alex while he remains in this apprenticeship
- This is a blanket rule for all English apprenticeships

### Possible Next Steps

If circumstances change, you may wish to reassess:
- **If Alex leaves the apprenticeship and enters full-time education** (such as A-levels, T-levels, or college courses) at a school or college rather than through an apprenticeship, he could potentially become eligible again
- **If Alex reaches age 20**, he would no longer qualify for Child Benefit anyway

### Further Help

If you have questions about this decision or your circumstances change, you can:
- Contact HMRC Child Benefit team
- Visit [www.gov.uk/child-benefit](https://www.gov.uk/child-benefit)

I'm sorry this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify?
